data.question: How well does SWOT RiverSP Version D reach water surface elevation follow the USGS gauge at Baton Rouge, and where does it not?

data.takes: SIGNED (human:PaulMRamirez). Rules in: pair each pass with a gauge reading inside a stated tolerance (15 minutes in the worked example), score the changes between consecutive pairs (mean error, RMSD, correlation, gauge change spread), with lag-1 sampling intervals capped at the count; name the collection. Rules out: scoring the level difference or calling it a bias (two vertical references, uncited offset); fewer than ten pairs; matching outside the tolerance; an unnamed collection. Warns: gauge is provisional throughout 2024; RMSD of the change is about four times the product's own median per-pass uncertainty. It already holds the 2024 all-pass change scores for this very pair, so exploring starts from those and asks where the disagreement sits. It says nothing about the quality flags or about a gain.

SIGNED (human:PaulMRamirez). Rules in: every statistic names its level; this question is reach level and the reach wse with its own wse_u is the product's authoritative aggregation. Rules out: quoting node statistics as reach ones. Warns: wse_u is total and wse_r_u random; reach_q and xovr_cal_q are categorical gates, not uncertainties.

NOT SIGNED (draft, working memory, written by claude-code/opus-5). About lakes, but the mechanism applies: the satellite is on a geoid and the gauge on a national datum, a constant unsourced offset appears in every pass and looks like a precise bias. Rules in: compare changes, not levels. Used as unsigned support for what the signed recipe already rules.

SIGNED (human:PaulMRamirez). About lakes; bears through the shared geoid: wse is above EGM2008 mean tide with tides removed; Version C had a geoid error fixed in D. Rules in: one family per series, family named. Warns: joining C and D gives a step. Here only Version D is used.

SIGNED (human:PaulMRamirez). Mostly lakes. The one fact used here: Version D is CRID PGD0 reprocessing for 2023-03-30 to 2025-04-27 and CRID PID0 forward processing from 2025-04-28 (from the Version D release note). So calendar 2024 is expected to be PGD0, and the data set aside from 2025-01-01 contains a PGD0 part (to 2025-04-27) and a PID0 part (from 2025-04-28). Also: quality flags are categorical gates; dark_frac is the fraction not directly detected; xovr_cal_q grades the crossover calibration. These field meanings are stated for lakes, and are carried to the river fields of the same name as an assumption.

SIGNED (human:PaulMRamirez, twice). Rules in: reach collection SWOT_L2_HR_RiverSP_reach_D named; elevation against a gauge is a confrontation (no gauge prior in wse). Rules out: using discharge against a gauge as independent. Warns: C family stops 2025-05-03, D carries forward processing and the CRID varies within the collection; reach_q, xovr_cal_q are gates, wse_u total and wse_r_u random. It does not say what the values of reach_q mean for rivers, nor the bit meanings of any bitwise flag.

SIGNED (human:PaulMRamirez). Rules in: name the collection on every request and record it. Warns: Version C and D differ by metres at this very reach (D spans -0.534 to 10.201 m in 2024 over 52 passes; the gauge 1.47 to 10.37 m above a datum at zero). So the working file must say it is Version D, and its minimum wse of -0.534 m sits about 2 m below the gauge minimum, which is worth finding by name.

SIGNED (human:PaulMRamirez, three times; its stale_after of 2026-11-01 has passed, so it is stale on the date of this work). Warns: gauge height is in FEET (parameter 00065), convert explicitly; continuous data is a rolling one year deep, so 2024 instantaneous stage came from a capture; times are UTC.

SIGNED (human:PaulMRamirez). About modelled daily flow, not this question. Takes only by analogy: score size and timing apart, one summary number hides where it fails, and a second period is a second row and not a wider interval.

SIGNED (human:PaulMRamirez, twice). Rules in: wse is on the EGM2008 geoid; cite Version D. Warns: fill values are large negatives and must be filtered, not averaged; reach and node series answer different questions.
SIGNED by human:PaulMRamirez but status draft. About lake identifiers; does not bear on a river reach keyed on one SWORD reach_id. Nothing taken beyond: read the quality and partial flags beside wse.
SIGNED (human:PaulMRamirez). Groundwater wells; listed by shared words only. Does not bear on this question; nothing taken.

SIGNED (human:PaulMRamirez, twice). Not listed by the tool; read because the recipe says the gauge is provisional throughout 2024. Warns: provisional values can be revised, so record the retrieval date of the gauge side and say the comparison rests on provisional stage.

data.text: The working file carries no processing identifier (CRID), cycle or pass number, xovr_cal_q or bitwise quality flag for any of its 52 passes. So it cannot be read from the data that calendar 2024 is all PGD0 (the signed swot-lakes page says it should be), a later window cannot be guarded against mixed processing from a file of this shape, the three overpass tracks had to be inferred from repeat-cycle phase (LOOK-011), and the reason for reach_q 2 on three passes cannot be seen. It also keeps only two hourly gauge readings around the passes of February and March (LOOK-009, LOOK-012), which is why two passes are unpaired at 15 minutes.

The recipe's worked example scores every paired pass and reads its change RMSD of 0.3823 m as about four times the product's stated precision. On the same 50 pairs, two passes carry 0.912 of the summed squared departure from the median difference (LOOK-004): 2024-10-30 (reach_q 2, wse_u 0.095 m, 1.776 m low, the year's lowest stage) and 2024-03-26 (reach_q 1, wse_u 0.296 m, dark_frac 0.692, 0.947 m high). With reach_q below 2 the change RMSD is 0.1859 m; with wse_u below 0.2 m as well it is 0.1051 m and the residual scatter (0.0815 m) is below the median stated uncertainty (0.0957 m) (LOOK-005, LOOK-010). The recipe's numbers are reproduced exactly (LOOK-003); what it lacks is any word on quality screening and on what reach_q values mean for a river reach. No page in the bundle says either. Seen on data already looked at: a lead for the steward, not a correction.

The page's stale_after is 2026-11-01 and this work ran on 2026-11-25, inside the window in which it says the legacy Water Services host closes. It is signed, and it was read as signed but stale. It bears here only through units (stage in feet) and the one-year depth of the continuous collection, which means a later study cannot fetch 15-minute stage older than a year from the new API.

Splitting passes by the minute of the pass time to tell overpass geometries apart gave 22 groups and said nothing. LOOK-011 regrouped by repeat-cycle phase and found three tracks with screened mean residuals of -0.0235, +0.0159 and +0.0051 m: no track stands out on this year.

alternatives: keep the mixed footing of LOOK-005, LOOK-008 and LOOK-011 (15 minutes nearest for one, 60 minutes interpolated for another, plain errors for some)
use 60 minutes interpolated for everything, which keeps all 52 passes
a block bootstrap for the intervals
data.choice: Answering REVIEW-001 hole 4: every gain compared in the revised lead is put on one footing before it is looked at again: the shipped pairing rule at 15 minutes nearest reading, the same pass set for every model within a row, and two kinds of interval printed side by side for every fit (plain least squares, and the same widened by the lag-1 effective sample of that fit's own residuals, capped at the count). Models: gauge alone; gauge and time; gauge and the product's reach slope; gauge, time and slope; and the gauge alone on the lower and upper halves of stage split at the median gauge elevation of the set.
data.rests_on: REVIEW-001 hole 4: the three fits in lead version 1 were not comparable. 15 minutes is the signed recipe's worked example and LOOK-009 found the pairing rule moves the screened gain by at most 0.003. Recorded before the look that uses it; the numbers of LOOK-005, 007, 008 and 011 were already seen, so the direction of the answer is known and only the footing is new.

alternatives: define a gross error as beyond 0.3 m, or beyond 5 robust standard deviations
judge only the 50 pairs of the 15 minute rule
also use rules that compare a pass with its neighbours in time (satellite only)
data.choice: Answering REVIEW-001 holes 1 and 5: for the look at what a screening rule would have to be, a gross error is fixed in advance as a pass whose satellite height departs by more than 0.5 m from a line that needs no screen (Theil-Sen slope over all passes, median intercept), on all 52 passes with the gauge interpolated inside 60 minutes so that every pass the product delivered is judged. Candidate rules are restricted to fields the product carries in the working file and that do not use the gauge: reach_q, wse_u, dark_frac, slope, width, ice_clim_f. For each field the look reports which passes a threshold removes at every possible cut, so the whole range of thresholds that would separate a gross error is seen and not one tuned value.
data.rests_on: LOOK-004 already listed every pass, so it is known before this look that two passes (2024-03-26 and 2024-10-30) will meet the definition and that the next largest departure is near 0.23 m: the 0.5 m line is drawn in a gap already seen, and the look reports 0.3 m beside it. The purpose is not to find the passes again but to see how many product-only rules catch them, at what cost in ordinary passes, and how wide the range of equally good thresholds is.

data.about: knowledge: meaning of reach_q values and the bitwise flag for RiverSP reach Version D (datasets/swot-river-lake.md)
data.text: No knowledge page says what the values of reach_q mean for a river reach. In the working year the flag is 1 on 49 of 52 passes and 2 on 3; no pass has 0 or 3 (LOOK-013). The signed lakes page gives the lake flag as 0 good, 1 suspect, 2 degraded, 3 bad; if the reach flag has the same ladder then every pass of 2024 at this reach is marked at least suspect, and nothing in the knowledge says why. The bitwise flag behind reach_q, the crossover calibration quality, and any field saying how much of the reach was observed are not in the working file. Wanted from the product description, by the steward: the value ladder for reach_q, the bits behind it, and which fields say that a reach was partly observed. A screen for a confirming study cannot be written from the knowledge as it stands. Extends NOTE-002.

data.about: knowledge/recipes/swot-gauge-confrontation.md (signed): the distance between reach and gauge
data.text: The signed recipe says the reach and the gauge are 0.44 km apart and does not say what the distance is measured to (the reach centre along the river, or the nearest point of the centreline) nor on which side. It matters: the product's reach slope rises by 3.179 ppm per metre of stage on the screened pairs, so each kilometre between the gauge and the point the reach height refers to adds 0.0032 to the gain. At 0.44 km geometry gives 0.0014 of the 0.0140 seen; 4.39 km would give all of it (LOOK-015). Wanted: the along-river distance and direction from the gauge to the reach centre, from SWORD and the site file, so that the gain expected from geometry is a number before any test.

The null it led to (no track stands out, three tracks of 15 to 17 screened passes in one year) is too thin to state about the product and is already in the lead. The reason the key was needed, no pass number in the file, is on the fixture page drafted from NOTE-001.
